prompt: Produce the 'variable is never used' warning an IDE greys out declarations with. Complete UnusedLocalFinder, then run the tests.
explanation: declaredName is a tiny hand-written parser: requiring the type token to be followed by a space is what separates "String s" from "Stringy s", and requiring '=' or ';' after the name is what rejects a for-loop header or a method call. The usage scan then skips the declaration line itself, so a variable that only appears where it is introduced is still reported -- including the pathological "long k = k;". containsIdentifier applies the whole-identifier rule, which is why declaring sum and returning sums still counts as unused.
hints: Keep the six type names in a List and loop over them; text.startsWith(type + " ") is the first gate.
After the type, read the identifier character by character, skip any spaces, and require the next character to be '=' or ';'.
When checking whether a name is used, skip the line that declares it -- and compare whole identifiers, so 'sums' does not count as a use of 'sum'.
